items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...composers like, say, Jilly Roll Morton or other people that were local? [INTERVIEWEE] Well, not where I played. They would request stardust and body and soul...

ctx.x: He wasn't my very best. Gershwin? Gershwin, yeah. I used to love to play that. You know, I've been out since 59, and there's this think tank going back on me, you know. Not too badly. You have to live in that life to keep up with it, you know. I knew a million tunes. We could play. We had so many composers in the band, and some nights the cars would play only our own tunes. Yeah, well I wrote a lot of tunes. Yeah, well I wrote a lot of tunes. They always wanted to, I wasn't smart. If I could give them Jack Mills…

You know what I mean? Do you think that the people here in New Orleans request a lot of the music that was particularly, say, associated with this area and by composers like, say, Jilly Roll Morton or other people that were local?

Well, not where I played. They would request stardust and body and soul and all that kind of stuff. Things that were nationally known. Something that was a must. You know what I mean? Like night and day was a must.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I'm sorry to say that I had very little knowledge of Jelly Roll.

ctx.x: Well, of course, you know and I know that the big band had a stay. It did have a stay, and they had good bands, very fine bands. But in spite of the fact that even when I used the big band, I always played Dixieland, you know, because I'd see some people who would never get on the floor unless you played two beats. I know a prominent man, a big man over the river. He'd be sitting at a supper dance and he wouldn't move and he'd be looking at me and I'd say, Johnny, when are you going to play my tune? So I'd say,…
How about things like, say, Mr. Jelly Lord. So you remember songs like that? Those old Jelly Roll Morton things?

I'm sorry to say that I had very little knowledge of Jelly Roll. He may have been the greatest. You see, my position is that I was working. And I knew what was around me. And I could only get a night off once in a while, you know, to go hear somebody else play. Did you ever hear A Sweetheart of Mine, that song? No. I know one thing. I believe I was the only orchestra that ever played My Wonderful One, written by Paul Whiteman. I believe that's the only tune he ever wrote, isn't it? I don't know if he really wrote…
